paras.text: O you who believe! Avoid much suspicion, for some suspicion is a sin; and do not spy into one another's affairs, and let none of you backbite anyone. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would surely hate it (so do not backbite) and fear Allah. Indeed Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.

Translation: Believers! Men should not mock (other) men; it is possible that those being mocked are better than them. Nor should women mock (other) women; it is possible that those being mocked are better than them. And do not find fault with one another, nor call one another by bad names. To give a bad name after believing is a sin. And those who do not repent, they are the wrongdoers.

O you who believe! Avoid much suspicion, for some suspicion is a sin; and do not spy into one another's affairs, and let none of you backbite anyone. Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would surely hate it (so do not backbite) and fear Allah. Indeed Allah is the Accepter of repentance, the Merciful.

Quranic teachings give the entire human society the lesson of complete protection of life and property. The unjust killing of one person has been declared the killing of humanity, and saving the life of one person has been described as saving the life of the whole of humanity.

Islam does not only take responsibility for protecting life and property, but also grants open permission for freedom of thought and freedom of opinion. In this regard the teachings of Islam are very clear.

The divine saying is:

لَآ اِكْرَاهَ فِي الدِّيْنِ

Translation: There is no compulsion in religion.

The Noble Prophet ﷺ placed the foundation of Islamic society on mutual love and brotherhood. His ﷺ blessed saying is:

By God, no one can be a believer until he likes for his brother the same that he likes for himself.

He ﷺ said that you people will not enter Paradise until you bring faith, and (you will not be believers) until you begin to love one another. (Sahih Muslim: 203)

Huzoor, the Noble Prophet ﷺ, did not only give the lesson of mutual love; rather he ﷺ also forbade Muslims from backbiting one another and from slandering.

عَنْ اَبِيْ هُرَيْرَةَ رَضِيَ اللّٰهُ عَنْهُ، اَنَّ رَسُوْلَ اللّٰهِ صَلَّى اللّٰهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهٖ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ: "اَتَدْرُوْنَ مَا الْغِيْبَةُ؟" قَالُوْا: اَللّٰهُ وَرَسُوْلُهٗ اَعْلَمُ. قَالَ: "ذِكْرُكَ اَخَاكَ بِمَا يَكْرَهُ" قِيْلَ: اَفَرَاَيْتَ اِنْ كَانَ فِيْ اَخِيْ مَا اَقُوْلُ؟ قَالَ: "اِنْ كَانَ فِيْهِ مَا تَقُوْلُ، فَقَدِ اغْتَبْتَهٗ، وَاِنْ لَّمْ يَكُنْ فِيْهِ مَا تَقُوْلُ فَقَدْ بَهَتَّهٗ" (رواہ مسلم)

Translation: It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you know what backbiting is?" The Companions submitted: Allah and His Messenger know best. The Noble Prophet ﷺ said: "Mentioning your brother in such a manner that he would dislike." The Noble Prophet ﷺ was asked: tell (us), if that thing is present in my brother which I mention? The Holy Messenger ﷺ said: "If that thing is present in him which you mention, then certainly you have backbitten him; and if that matter is not in him which you state about him, then you have slandered him."
